1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7.name: French Defence: Classical Variation, Normal Variation
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7.background: The line 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e5 Nfd7 6.Bxe7 Qxe7 used to be the main line of the French Defence; the Burn Variation (4...dxe4) has since overtaken 4...Be7 in popularity.

1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e5.strategy: Pushes the pawn with a gain of time, since it attacks the knight and so answers the unpinning with a threat of its own. White commits to a cramping pawn chain and a space advantage, and Black must find counterplay against the centre.

1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.Bx.strategy: Takes the knight that attacks e4, so the pawn can stay where it is. White gives up the bishop pair, and Black recaptures with a bishop that eyes d4. White plays for a solid centre rather than a cramping pawn chain.
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.Bx.name: French Defence: Classical Variation, Richter Attack

1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.Bx.strategy: The natural recapture: Black keeps healthy pawns and the bishop pair, and the bishop on f6 eyes the d4 pawn along the long diagonal. Taking with the g-pawn would hand White a lasting target on the kingside.

1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e5.strategy: The main retreat: the knight leaves the attacked square for one from which it hits the e5 pawn and helps to undermine the chain. The cost is a cramped position with the c8 bishop shut in, but Black has a firm structure and a clear plan against the centre.

Counterattacks the c3 knight and offers exchanges to ease the cramp. If the pieces come off, White's queen can swing to g4, hitting the e4 pawn and g7 at once, so Black has to defend accurately. It frees the game at the price of a pawn on e4 that is hard to hold.
1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e5.name: French Defence: Classical Variation, Tartakower Variation

1.e4 e6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e5.strategy: Takes the knight all the way home, losing two tempi for a modest idea: to recapture on e7 with the knight if the bishops are traded. White simply keeps the bishop and enjoys the extra space and a big lead in development.
